steps.title: Bearing into the base
steps.note: Press on the outer ring only, evenly (flat block + vise)
steps.fit: Ø47.1 mm press fit. Bearing into the base pocket. Too tight: sand the pocket wall a little at a time. Loose: 1 layer of tape.
steps.how: Push on the OUTER ring only, evenly: flat block on top, squeeze in a vise or press with both thumbs. No glue.

callouts.text: pocket Ø47.1 · press fit: sand the wall

steps.title: Turntable servo
steps.note: From underneath; body points away from the arm side
steps.how: 4 x #8-32 screws from UNDERNEATH: through the 4 holes in the servo's tabs, up into the 2 printed blocks inside the base. They cut their own thread in the plastic: snug, don't over-tighten (it strips).

steps.title: Weight + feet
steps.note: ~100 g in the 2 back pockets (washers, pennies, rocks): GLUE or TAPE it in. 4 feet or hot-glue dots
steps.how: ~50 g of washers / coins / small rocks in each back pocket, glued in. Optional: 4 rubber feet or hot-glue dots under the base.
steps.glue_text: Hot glue or tape the washers into the 2 back pockets: the pockets are open underneath, loose weight just stays on the table.

steps.title: Servo horn
steps.note: Set the servo to 135° first (servo_setup: t 135)
steps.how: Turn the servo to 135° first (laptop panel: Base 135, or servo_setup: t 135). Press the round horn onto the spline with its 4 inner holes on the diagonals (45°, 135°…), as close as the spline teeth allow, then the small centre screw from the servo bag.

steps.title: Turret plate
steps.note: Hub into the bearing; rod bosses point at the START can. Turns 90° freely
steps.fit: Ø34.95 mm press fit. Hub into the bearing's inner ring. Too tight: sand the hub evenly while turning it. The plate must turn freely after.
steps.how: The hub drops into the bearing's inner ring and covers the horn (the horn sits inside the hub). Turn the horn until its 4 holes line up with the 4 holes in the plate, then drive 4 servo-bag screws DOWN through the plate into the horn. Tip: open the plate's 4 holes to 3/32″ (2.4 mm) first, so the screws bite only the horn and pull the plate down onto it. No glue: the 4 screws carry the turning force, the bearing carries the weight (the plate's shoulder rests on the inner ring) and the hub keeps it centred. The plate looks small next to the bearing because the bearing does the holding. If your horn has no holes on that circle: use the plate as a drill guide, 1.5 mm pilots through the horn. Superglue only if the hub is loose in the bearing.

callouts.text: hub Ø34.95 · press fit: sand the hub

steps.title: Linear bearings into the carriage
steps.note: 2 from below, 2 from above, flush with the faces
steps.fit: Ø12.15 mm press fit ×4, in line. Pockets print on their side: ream with a 12 mm drill or sandpaper on a dowel until each LM6UU presses in.
steps.how: Do this on the table, carriage on its own: 2 bearings from below, 2 from above, flush with the faces. Press with a flat block. No glue (a drop of superglue only if one is loose).

callouts.text: pocket Ø12.15 · 12 mm bit / sandpaper on a dowel

steps.title: Carriage onto the rods (on the table)
steps.note: Slide both rods down through the 4 bearings. Tilt it: the carriage must slide by its own weight
steps.fit: Slide test. Rods through all 4 bearings; tilt the rods: the carriage must slide down by its own weight, no tight spot. Sticks: ream the tight pocket a little.
steps.how: Still on the table: slide both 6 mm rods down through the carriage's 4 bearings, so the carriage rides on the rods. Leave the same length of rod sticking out under the carriage on both sides.

steps.title: Rods + carriage into the turret plate
steps.note: Press both rod ends into the blind holes, straight down, carriage on the rods
steps.fit: Ø6.0 mm press fit. Rod ends into the turret plate's blind holes, straight down to the bottom. Too tight: open the holes with a 6 mm (or 15/64″) bit turned by hand.
steps.how: Hold the rods (carriage on them) upright and press both rod ends into the turret plate's 2 blind holes at the same time. No screws, no glue: the top cap traps the rods in step 10.

callouts.text: blind hole Ø6.0 · 6 mm or 15/64″ bit

steps.title: Spine
steps.note: Onto the turret plate behind the rods, screws from above
steps.how: 2 x #6-32 from ABOVE through the spine's foot into the turret plate (self-threading).

steps.title: Top cap
steps.note: Over the rod tops onto the spine. Carriage still slides freely?
steps.fit: Try-fit Ø6.0 mm, both rods. Cap over the rod tops: tight → drill 6 mm (15/64″) by hand, 8 mm deep. Then the 2 screws. After: the carriage must still slide freely.
steps.how: 2 x #6-32 from ABOVE through the cap into the top of the spine.

callouts.text: blind hole Ø6.0 · 6 mm or 15/64″ bit, 8 mm deep

steps.title: Lift servo
steps.note: Body through the spine bracket from the left
steps.how: Servo body through the bracket from the left, 2 servo-bag screws through its tabs into the bracket.

steps.title: Lift link
steps.note: Carriage end: #6-32 as the pivot, don't over-tighten: it must turn
steps.fit: Ø3.9 mm running fit. The link must swing freely on the screw. Binds: open the hole with a 5/32 in drill turned by hand.
steps.how: #6-32 through the link into the carriage's small boss: it is the pivot. Stop as soon as it is snug, then back off 1/4 turn so the link turns.

steps.title: Crank
steps.note: Single-arm horn trimmed to 20 mm, on the spline at 30°; pin screw into the link
steps.fit: This joint must turn. Drill the link's small hole to 3/32″ (2.4 mm) so the link turns on the screw; the screw threads into the horn hole only. 20 mm from the horn centre to that hole.
steps.how: Lift servo at 30° first. Horn on the spline + its centre screw. Then a servo-bag screw from the OUTSIDE: through the link (opened to 2.4 mm), into the horn's hole at 20 mm. The screw head holds the link on; the link pivots on the screw.

steps.title: Wrist servo
steps.note: Body through the bracket from the front
steps.how: Body through the arm's bracket from the front, 2 servo-bag screws through the tabs.

steps.title: Wrist horn
steps.how: Wrist servo at 0° first. Round horn on the spline, holes on the diagonals, centre screw.

steps.title: Gripper frame
steps.note: Upright: plates level, opening facing out
steps.how: 4 servo-bag screws through the frame's flange into the horn (open the flange holes to 3/32″ / 2.4 mm first, so the screws pull the frame onto the horn). Plates level, opening facing out.

steps.title: Both fingers, gears meshed
steps.note: Slide them in together between the plates, open by the same angle
steps.fit: Gear mesh: try it on. Teeth engage with a little play and no binding over the full swing. Never sand or file gear teeth. Printers rarely print teeth exactly, so the file is made to be edited: if they bind, print the looser pair (cad/print/stl/finger_variants/, gear_thin 0.18 or 0.25); if they rattle, the tighter pair (0.00). Or set gear_thin in backend/cad/model.py and run backend/cad/finger_variants.py.
steps.how: Slide both fingers in together between the plates, both opened by the same angle, so the teeth mesh symmetrically.

steps.title: Right finger axle
steps.note: From the top through the right finger; it must swing freely
steps.fit: Ø3.9 mm running fit. The finger must swing freely on the axle. Tight: twist a 5/32 in drill through by hand.
steps.how: #6-32 from the top through the frame and the right finger, threading into the bottom plate: it is the axle.

steps.title: Horn on the left gear, then the gripper servo
steps.note: Horn flat on the left gear, 2 screws; then the servo's spline down into the horn hub
steps.fit: Horn trimmed to Ø12 mm, flat on the gear. Cut the SG90 round horn down to Ø12 mm (flush cutters, then sand), keeping its 2 holes 5 mm from the centre (or drill 1.5 mm through the horn using the gear's pilots as the guide). A full-size horn hits the servo post. The spline must slide into the hub without force.
steps.how: 1) Open both fingers the same amount. Lay the trimmed SG90 round horn (Ø12) flat on the left finger's gear, hub UP, and drive 2 servo-bag screws through it into the gear's 2 pilots. 2) Gripper servo at 20° first (laptop panel). 3) Lower the servo so its spline goes into the horn hub, then 2 servo-bag screws through its tabs into the frame's posts. The finger can't drop off: it sits 0.5 mm above the bottom plate and the spline is 2.5 mm deep in the hub. Same idea as the earlier prototype gripper.

callouts.text: horn screws → pilots Ø1.7, 5 mm from centre

steps.title: Can bumper
steps.note: Silicone or rubber, 9 × 13.5 mm, superglue to the frame
steps.how: Cut 9 x 13.5 mm from the silicone sheet (or a rubber band / inner tube).
steps.glue_text: Superglue the rubber pad to the frame where the can's side touches.

steps.title: Electronics on the tray
steps.note: Pegs + a dab of hot glue; breadboard is self-adhesive. Buck already set to 5.8 V
steps.how: Boards onto the printed pegs. Buck already set to 5.8 V (bench test).
steps.glue_text: A dab of hot glue on each peg holds the Uno and the buck. The breadboard is self-adhesive.

steps.title: Panel: button, LED, power
steps.note: Through the panel holes from the front, nuts inside. Power: DC jack, or the LIZVOR terminal-block tip
steps.how: Button, LED and DC jack go through the panel holes from the front; their nuts go on inside.

steps.title: Tray onto the base
steps.note: Tabs slide under the base wall, screws from below
steps.how: Tabs slide under the base wall, then 2 x #6-32 from UNDERNEATH through the tabs into the base.

names.gripper_horn: SG90 round horn, trimmed to Ø12 mm

precise.label: PRECISE FIT
precise.text: Press fits and alignment that decide whether the robot works. They depend on how your printer prints holes: print and check the tolerance coupon (plate A) first, then measure with calipers. Do these last, with the parts in hand.

try.label: TRY-FIT
try.text: Test before you tighten: it should turn, slide or mesh freely. Easy to fix with a drill bit by hand, a knife or sandpaper.

easy.label: EASY
easy.text: Screws into servo tabs, glue, boards on pegs. Any print quality works: do these while the precise parts are still printing.

while_waiting: Electronics bench test (PART E) and set the buck to 5.8 V
Set every servo to its angle (laptop panel) before it gets its horn
Cut the 2 rods to 112 mm, file the ends
Cut a single-arm horn to a 20 mm hole radius (step 13)
Cut the rubber pad 9 x 13.5 mm (step 20)
Print the electronics tray first (plate C, draft) and do steps 21-22
Servos into their brackets as soon as each printed part arrives (steps 2, 11, 14)
